title: Explaining away
sub: Exact posteriors in a three-node Bayesian network with a collider.

frames.caption: Two independent causes of one effect: flu and allergy can each cause a runny nose. Before any evidence: flu 10%, allergy 20%. Learning about one tells you nothing about the other: they are independent.
Suppose we learn the patient has flu. Allergy stays at 20%: with the nose unobserved, the path flu → nose ← allergy is blocked at the collider.
Start over, and instead observe a runny nose. Both causes become more likely: flu rises to 34%, allergy to 59%.

Now also learn that the patient has flu. Allergy drops from 59% to 23%, close to where it started: the flu already explains the runny nose. Observing the collider made two independent causes dependent. That is explaining away, and it is why conditioning on a common effect (as selection bias does) creates spurious correlations.
And if instead the patient is known not to have flu, allergy jumps to 78%: something has to explain the nose.
